thread:
maya: quick follow-up on the admission/provenance discussion from the RFC thread — who should own the 'provenance' blob that flows into the fairness scheduler? we need a clear contract for tracing abuse signals into scheduling decisions.

sam: my take: admission should attach provenance when it issues a lease. keeps the routing layer stateless and lets downstream schedulers reason about why a request got lower priority.

liam: agree in principle but concern: payload bloat + accidental leakage of internal signals to other subsystems. we should define a minimal schema and strongly type what can be included. no raw PII.

alex: proposed minimal contract (sketch):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "lease_id": "l-456",
  "credits": 10,
  "provenance": {
    "source": "abuse-detector-v2",
    "score": 0.87,
    "bucket": "spike-1m",
    "version": "2026-03-01"
  }
}
```
keep it small and stable.

nisha: +1 for stable fields. telemetry note: we should emit metrics tagged by provenance.source and provenance.version so quality/regression alerts can correlate changes in scheduling with upstream model updates.

sam: rollout plan idea: start opt-in behind a feature flag that adds header `X-Admission-Provenance: 1` and only route those through the new scheduler path. fallback remains current behavior.

maya: security ask from abuse team: do not include raw client IPs, user identifiers, or full request bodies in provenance. allow hashed identifiers with tenant-scoped salt. record the salt rotation policy in the docs.

liam: also consider retention/TTL for provenance: I propose 24h by default, configurable per-tenant. long retention increases storage/ingest costs and risk surface.

alex: ops integration: provenance should be surfaced in traces but redacted in logs unless request is opt-in with audit justification. example sampling config:
```yaml
tracing:
  sample_rate: 0.1
  include_provenance_in_trace: true
  redact_in_logs: true
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary: admission-provenance-canary -> tomorrow 09:00 UTC :rocket:

nisha: one more thing — API for downstream consumers: provide a small helper lib that normalizes provenance fields across languages (go/py/node). avoids subtle mismatches in how score/version are parsed.

sam: agreed. action items: (1) draft compact provenance schema and publish in API repo (sam), (2) add feature-flagged header and opt-in rollout plan (maya), (3) telemetry tags + dashboard for provenance variants (nisha), (4) helper libs + docs (alex), (5) security review for hashing/salt rotation (liam). I'll open the PRs tomorrow.

maya: great — I'll coordinate the canary with SRE and the abuse team. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

liam: tiny follow-up — does anyone object to the 24h default TTL?

nisha: fine from telemetry POV. longer retention can be enabled per enterprise contract.

alex: sounds good. i'll create the initial schema RFC and link it in this thread when done.

maya: closing loop: once alex posts the schema RFC we'll merge action item owners into that doc and schedule the canary.

sam: ack.
